title: Error Handling
description: Learn how to catch, classify, and report errors in Next.js APIs so users see helpful messages and you can debug production issues quickly.

data.text: Every API endpoint will encounter errors: bad input, missing records, database timeouts, or unexpected bugs. Good error handling turns these moments into useful feedback instead of confusing crashes.

Not all errors are the same. Client errors mean the caller did something wrong, like sending an invalid ID. Server errors mean something broke inside your code. Knowing the difference determines the HTTP status code you return.

items: Client error: bad input, missing fields, or invalid authentication
Not found: the requested resource does not exist
Conflict: the request cannot be completed because of current state
Server error: unexpected exception, database down, or unhandled case

data.text: Creating custom error classes lets you attach extra information like an HTTP status code or error code. You can then catch these errors at the top level and format them consistently.

data.title: Custom API error classes

data.text: Wrap endpoint logic in a try/catch block. If you catch a known `APIError`, return its status and message. If you catch an unknown error, log it and return a 500 to avoid leaking internals.

data.title: Centralized error handling in a Route Handler
Log Everything, Expose Nothing
data.text: Always log the full error object on the server with `console.error` or a proper logger. The client should only see a generic message. Detailed logs let you fix issues without exposing secrets or stack traces to users.

Next.js lets you define global error files that catch errors from entire route segments. For API routes, you can also use middleware or a wrapper function to avoid repeating try/catch in every handler.

data.title: Reusable async wrapper for Route Handlers
Key Takeaways
items: Separate client errors from server errors and return the right status code
Use custom error classes to carry status codes and error codes
Log full error details server-side; return generic messages to clients
Wrap handlers in a reusable function to avoid repetitive try/catch
